result.title: ACUS: An Angular Calibrated Uncertainty Score for Incomplete-View CT
result.summary: Sparse-view and limited-arc computed tomography (CT) are commonly treated as projection completion: a network fills an unmeasured view, and the result is ranked by similarity to one ground-truth image. That score can be high even when the query angle is far from every acquired measurement, because a learned prior may invent anatomy the scan never constrained. Existing protocols therefore leave a basic question unanswered: how does predictive reliability change with distance from the acquired views? We propose the Angular Calibrated Uncertainty Score (ACUS) to answer that question. ACUS is the Winkler interval score of a nominal 90% predictive interval on held-out projections, binned by distance to the nearest acquired view. It charges interval width and adds a large miss penalty when a held-out pixel falls outside the interval, so a narrow band helps only when coverage holds. We use collapse on acquired angles as a necessary consistency check on the predictor. On chest and dental cone-beam orbits, interval width grows with the angular gap. Empirical coverage ranges from 77% to 92%, and the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of the point estimate falls as the width rises. Nearest-neighbor, interpolation, and point completion, each given one residual scale, have zero reported far coverage and incur outside-distance penalties. ACUS exposes gap-dependent overconfidence that a point-estimate PSNR alone does not measure.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对稀疏视角、有限弧 CT 提出 ACUS 指标：对留出投影上的 90% 预测区间按「到最近已采集视角的角度距离」分箱计算 Winkler 区间分数，同时惩罚区间宽度与覆盖失败，用以揭示点估计 PSNR 无法反映的、随视角缺口增大的过度自信。
AI.relevance_reason: 「按与已获证据的距离分层校准可靠性、并惩罚窄而不覆盖的区间」这一思路，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据不足程度与停止决策（STOP）的风险度量提供可核查的评估借鉴。
